language.why: A difference card shows free-molecule, gas-phase ESP. Words that suggest a biological mechanism, or that overlapping ranges mean 'the same', turn a measurement into a claim nobody tested; and every comparable card should say what the number is of.

cases.why: Same molecule pair, one ensemble computed under another protocol: def2-TZVP moves C18 V_max by +1.5 to +2.8 kcal/mol, the size of the differences taught. Any number compared across analysis keys is a protocol difference shown as a chemical one.

Same molecule pair, one ensemble computed under another protocol: PCM water moves chlorobenzene's V_max by -3.60 under one convention and +0.05 under the other. Any number compared across analysis keys is a protocol difference shown as a chemical one.
19 conformers share a key and one does not (a re-run added to the folder). Averaging it in silently mixes protocols; the stray member must stop the comparison.
As above, the stray member in the second molecule, last in the list.
One conformer each, different keys. Both refusals are safe; 'not compared' names the real problem, 'single conformer' hides it behind a lesser one.

With one conformer on either side there is no conformer range to beat; a large difference between two single conformers is routine for a C18 chain (pilot ranges 2.5-6.2). A range of 0.00 printed for n = 1 reads as 'no variation', which is false.

All 10 v 10 separate, but only because A's two folded conformers sit at its low end; over extended conformers the ranges overlap. 'Separated' alone teaches that the molecules differ, when their extended shapes do not (CLAUDE.md: extrema are robust only while nothing folds).
The reverse: extended conformers separate, one folded outlier makes the full ranges overlap. 'Overlapping' is the honest all-member answer; the card must still show the extended picture.
Only one of A's conformers is extended: there is no extended range to show, and the card must say so, not print a range of 0.00.
In one folded conformer the site has no surface (mean None). Dropping it silently changes n; averaging fails. The view should say the site is buried in that conformer.
The site is buried in every conformer of both molecules: there is nothing to compare.

The means differ consistently but the ranges overlap: some single conformations of the two molecules are indistinguishable. 'Overlapping' is right; a card that then reads as 'no difference' or 'identical' is false (frozen plan section 5, 'unresolved').

An infinite mean in the second molecule: the same refusal.
Finite under nearest-nucleus, NaN under radius-scaled: the sign test and the partition sensitivity both need the second rule, so the comparison is not measured.
No conformers on one side (a filter removed them all, a load found none). There is nothing to compare, and the refusal must say which side is empty.

cases.why: Delta_rs is -2.2e-16: rounding noise in the means, not a direction. Calling it rule-dependent tells a student the convention flips a +3.0 difference.
Delta_rs is -0.01: small, but a real opposite sign the card can print.
Delta_rs is -0.005, exactly the stated tolerance: a rule that says '0.005 or more' must count it whatever the last bit of the float subtraction is.
Delta_rs is -0.004, which the card prints as -0.00: either reading is defensible, so no preference; only OVERLAPPING is wrong.

Every mean is finite, but one conformer's partition sensitivity is nan. A partition is |difference between the two rules' means|: not finite, or negative, means the record is corrupt, and the comparison must stop, naming the conformer.

Two of A's conformers are folded by an intramolecular contact but their surfaces have genus 0. They drive the separation; the extended view must leave them out (n = 8 / 10).
Every conformer's surface has genus 1 (a macrocycle's hole), and none is folded. Treating genus as folding would empty the extended set; there is nothing to leave out.
A compound nobody tested shows as 'not tested', never as a negative result.
Tested with no detectable effect is a negative result, and must not be shown as untested.
An effect reported without a test is still an observation; the card shows 'significance not reported' beside it, not a stronger or weaker state.
Two studies on one taxon point opposite ways: show both, labelled contested, never the newer one alone.
The aldehyde control is constructed, not found in any Sesiidae: labelling it observed invents evidence.
A structure computed to ask 'what if' is a model, and is never shown as observed.
A trap catch and an antennal response to the same pair are different evidence; one merged 'active' badge erases which was measured.
Two populations of one species responding differently is a population difference, not noise to average.
A resolved ESP difference shown next to a species-specific response must not be joined to it by 'because', 'explains' or an arrow: nothing here tests the link.
Two ESP pictures with different colour scales side by side: the same colour means different kcal/mol, so the eye compares the wrong things.
A folded and an extended conformer side by side read as two molecules' shapes, not as one molecule's conformational range.
